class.name: PhysXGranular3D
class.brief_description: A GPU granular volume simulated by the PhysX physics backend -- sand, gravel or snow.
class.description: Fills [member PhysXParticleFluid3D.spawn_region_size] (or streams via [member PhysXParticleFluid3D.emitting]) with particles that behave as grains rather than a liquid: they pile up, hold a slope up to [member friction], and get plowed and cratered by bodies moving through them. Everything else -- emission, [member PhysXParticleFluid3D.mpm_colliders] / [member PhysXParticleFluid3D.mpm_auto_colliders], the domain, the [MultiMesh] render, the [RID] lifecycle -- is inherited from [PhysXParticleFluid3D]. There is no isosurface; grains are always drawn as the sphere [MultiMesh], with [member GeometryInstance3D.material_override] applied. The [b]MPM[/b] compute solver is the one that holds a real angle of repose -- PhysX's PBD particle friction cannot pile -- so [member PhysXParticleFluid3D.solver] set to [code]Auto[/code] always resolves to MPM here (which also runs on any GPU, no CUDA needed). Choose [code]PBD (CUDA)[/code] explicitly only for a pure pour or cascade where the grains stay in motion and never need to hold a shape.

members.member: Bulk density of the medium in kg/m³ -- the "weight" of the grains. It scales how hard a body has to work to plough through: light powder snow is around [code]300[/code], dry sand around [code]1500[/code], wet or packed sand higher. It does not change the angle of repose (that is [member friction]) or how fast a pile settles.

Internal friction angle in degrees -- the steepest slope a pile holds. The continuum discretisation loses a few degrees to free-surface creep, so set this a little above the angle of repose you actually want (dry sand is ~34, gravel ~45).
[code]0[/code] is dry sand. Small values pack the grains like wet sand or snow, letting a pile hold a steeper face and a light object rest on top instead of sinking.
Young's modulus of the grains, in pascals. Softer settles mushier and is more numerically forgiving; stiffer resists deformation but can jitter. The solver already forces extra substeps for granular.
